newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma City bombing lawyers spar over testimony.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma City bombing lawyers spar over testimony.

text.p: The lead prosecutor in the Oklahoma City bombing case denied Thursday defence claims that the government acted improperly in the way it handled information from a key witness.
"The government lawyers were beyond reproach and the FBI agents were an honourable group," prosecutor Joseph Hartzler told a pre-trial hearing.

Hartzler urged U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch not to throw out a portion of the testimony of Thomas Manning, a tire dealer in Junction City, Kansas that prosecutors said linked McVeigh to renting the Ryder truck allegedly used in the bombing.
Several days before the bombing Manning sold Timothy McVeigh the 1977 Mercury Marquis he was driving when he was arrested near Perry, Oklahoma 90 minutes after the bombing.
McVeigh and former army buddy Terry Nichols are charged with bombing the Alfred P. Murray federal building in 1995 that killed 168 people.
In a sworn deposition Manning testified that McVeigh left the tire store for a short while, during which time the government claimed he called a Ryder truck rental office.
Manning's deposition was taped because prosecutors said he had a life-threatening heart condition.
Defence lawyers want the testimony about McVeigh leaving the store suppressed because Manning did not mention it for 18 months, despite a series of interviews with prosecutors.

McVeigh's attorney Robert Nigh argued that prosecutors either improperly suggested to Manning "what his testimony should be" or that the government's earlier questioning of Manning "was extremely shoddy."
Defence lawyers want Manning's testimony thrown because of the prosecutors' alleged failure to inform them of Manning's supposedly inconsistent statements.
But prosecutors contend Manning's statements were not inconsistent because he had never been asked specifically whether McVeigh left the store briefly.
Matsch said he would decide later whether to suppress Manning's testimony. McVeigh's trial begins March 31. Nichols will be tried later at an undetermined date.
